derivations.claim: By [F3]–[F4], $f$ is totally differentiable and continuous on $V$, with state derivative matrix $D_yf$. On each open convex fiber $V_t$, the derivative bound and [F5]–[F6] make $f(t,\cdot)$ $L$-Lipschitz. Thus the hypotheses of [F7] hold and the IVP has a unique maximal solution; the given solution agrees with it throughout $[0,T]$.

Fix any $t\in[0,T)$ and $h>0$ with $t+h\le T$ satisfying the stated compact-set condition, and fix a component $i$. Define $g_i(s):=f_i(t+s,y(t+s))$ for $0\le s\le h$. The exact path segment lies in $K\subset V$, so [F8] gives $|g_i'(s)|\le B_i$ on $(0,h)$.
For each $s\in(0,h]$, [F10] applied to $g_i$ on $[0,s]$ yields $|g_i(s)-g_i(0)|\le B_i s$; at $s=0$ the same inequality is equality.

Apply [F9] to the IVP restarted at $(t,y(t))$; then $y_i(t+h)-y_i(t)=\int_0^h g_i(s)\,ds$. Euler's output from the exact state is $y_i(t)+hg_i(0)$, so $\delta_{h,i}(t;y)=\int_0^h(g_i(0)-g_i(s))\,ds$. Using [step 2.1] gives $|\delta_{h,i}(t;y)|\le\int_0^h B_i s\,ds=B_i h^2/2$. Squaring the component bounds, summing, and using [F11] gives the asserted Euclidean norm estimate. Its constant is independent of $t$ and $h$, proving uniform local order one under [F1].

For any admitted $t\in[0,T]$, $h>0$, and $u,v\in V_t$, [F3] identifies the derivative of $z\mapsto f(t,z)$ with $D_yf(t,z)$; [F5]–[F6] give $\|f(t,u)-f(t,v)\|_2\le L\|u-v\|_2$. Therefore [F12] gives $\|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)\|_2\le\|u-v\|_2+h\|f(t,u)-f(t,v)\|_2\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|_2$, which is the one-step stability bound in [F1] for inputs in $K$.

derivations.claim: Fix $T>0$, let $R:=e^T(1+T)+1$, and take $V=(-1,T+1)\times(-R,R)$ and $K=[0,T]\times[-R+1,R-1]$. These are an open domain with convex state fibers and a compact subset $K\subset V$. For $f(t,z)=z$, the bounds in [F2] hold throughout $V$ with $F_1=R$, $M_{t,1}=0$, $M_{11}=1$, and $L=1$. The function $y(t)=e^t$ solves the IVP, its graph on $[0,T]$ lies in $K$, and for every $0<h\le T-t$ the Euler output state $e^t(1+h)$ lies between $0$ and $e^T(1+T)=R-1$, so its input and output pairs lie in $K$. Starting from $e^t$, Euler returns $e^t(1+h)$ and the exact endpoint is $e^{t+h}=e^te^h$. Therefore [F1] gives $\delta_h(t;y)=e^t(1+h-e^h)$.
Apply [F3] to $s\mapsto e^s$ at $0$ with increment $h$: there is $\theta_h\in(0,h)$ with $e^h=1+h+\tfrac12 e^{\theta_h}h^2$. Thus $|\delta_h(t;y)|=\tfrac12 e^{t+\theta_h}h^2$.

Since $0<\theta_h<h$, for $0\le t\le T-h$ we have $\tfrac12h^2\le |\delta_h(t;y)|\le \tfrac12e^T h^2$. The lower and upper bounds establish uniform $\Theta(h^2)$ error, hence order exactly one under [F1].
For any scalar inputs $u,v$, $|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)|=|(1+h)(u-v)|=(1+h)|u-v|$. This verifies the stated stability factor; it also agrees with [F2] for $f(t,z)=z$ and $L=1$.

derivations.claim: For $t<0$, $y(t)=-t^2/2$ and $y'(t)=-t=|t|$; for $t>0$, $y(t)=t^2/2$ and $y'(t)=t=|t|$. At $t=0$, $\lim_{s\to0}(y(s)-y(0))/s=\lim_{s\to0}|s|/2=0=|0|$. Hence $y$ is the exact solution through $y(0)=0$.

At $t_h=-h/2$, the exact value is $y(t_h)=-h^2/8$ and the explicit midpoint stage time is $0$, where $f(0,z)=0$ for every stage value $z$. Thus $M_h(t_h,y(t_h))=y(t_h)=-h^2/8$, while $y(t_h+h)=y(h/2)=h^2/8$.

Therefore $\delta_h(t_h;y)=-h^2/4$. The exact segment has $|t|\le h/2\le1/2$ and $|y(t)|\le1/8$; the input and output states are $-h^2/8$, and the midpoint stage state is $h^2/8$, all in $[-1,1]$. Their time coordinates also lie in $[-1,1]$, so the definition applies on the fixed compact set $K$. If a uniform order-two bound held, $h^2/4\le Ch^3$ for every $0<h\le1$, forcing $C\ge1/(4h)$ as $h\downarrow0$, which is impossible.

For an arbitrary $t\in\mathbb R$ and $h>0$, the method increment from the exact state is $h|t+h/2|$. If $[t,t+h]$ lies on either side of $0$, then $y$ is quadratic there and this increment equals $y(t+h)-y(t)$, so the defect is zero. If $t<0<t+h$, put $r=-t/h\in(0,1)$. Using $y(t)=-t^2/2$ and $y(t+h)=(t+h)^2/2$ gives $\delta_h(t;y)=-h^2r^2$ for $0<r\le1/2$ and $\delta_h(t;y)=-h^2(1-r)^2$ for $1/2\le r<1$. Thus every crossing step has $|\delta_h(t;y)|\le h^2/4$, and the same bound holds for every step. In particular, it holds uniformly for all admitted starts and steps in $K$; together with step 3.1, the uniform local order is exactly one.
